notes: The keyword-metric-selector-workaround card tests the reserved-keyword parse conflict to avoid repeating r1's __name__ fact.

cards.statement: A Prometheus scrape job can combine static_configs with service discovery.
cards.explanation: Prometheus accepts both target sources in one job, so its target list can include configured and discovered endpoints.

cards.statement: Prometheus waits for a configuration reload before applying file-discovery target changes.
cards.explanation: Prometheus watches discovery files and applies valid target-group changes as they arrive.
cards.misconception: File-based discovery updates depend on reloading the main configuration.

cards.statement: Prometheus processes target relabeling steps in their listed configuration order.
cards.explanation: For targets still retained, later relabeling steps see labels changed by earlier steps.

cards.statement: Prometheus retains discovery __meta_ labels in the final labels attached to scraped samples.
cards.explanation: Prometheus removes discovery __meta_ labels after target relabeling; copying a value into a regular label preserves that metadata.
cards.misconception: Discovery metadata labels become ordinary scraped-series labels automatically.

cards.statement: For TCP scrapes, Prometheus uses the relabeled __address__ as the target address.
cards.explanation: Changing __address__ during target relabeling redirects the scrape to the resulting host and port.

cards.statement: Prometheus uses __param_target to set the target HTTP request header during a scrape.
cards.explanation: __param_target controls the first target URL query parameter. Prometheus encodes that parameter into the scrape URL.
cards.misconception: Internal parameter labels configure HTTP request headers.

cards.statement: Prometheus scrapes a target before a matching target relabeling drop rule removes it.
cards.explanation: Target drop rules match concatenated source_labels values and remove matching targets before scraping begins.
cards.misconception: Target filtering happens after Prometheus collects the target's metrics.

cards.statement: Prometheus's replace action expands regex capture groups in a replacement value.
cards.explanation: A replacement such as ${1} inserts text captured from the concatenated source_labels values.

cards.statement: Prometheus's labelkeep action tests its regex against label values to select labels.
cards.explanation: labelkeep evaluates label names. Prometheus retains the names that match and removes labels with other names.
cards.misconception: labelkeep selects labels by matching their contents.

cards.statement: Prometheus can drop its generated up series with metric_relabel_configs before ingestion.
cards.explanation: Metric relabeling filters scraped samples before ingestion. Prometheus excludes generated series such as up.
cards.misconception: Metric relabeling also filters Prometheus's generated scrape series.

cards.statement: Prometheus uses write_relabel_configs to choose which samples reach a remote write endpoint.
cards.explanation: Write relabeling filters the outgoing sample stream before Prometheus transmits it to that remote destination.

cards.statement: Prometheus adds external labels before applying alert_relabel_configs to outgoing alerts.
cards.explanation: Alert relabeling sees external labels, so it can normalize outgoing labels before delivery to Alertmanager.

cards.statement: Prometheus documentation favors an exporter for exposing metrics from application code you control.
cards.explanation: Prometheus recommends client-library instrumentation inside applications whose code you control.
cards.misconception: An exporter is preferred for code developers own.

cards.statement: The Prometheus docs recommend collecting exporter values when Prometheus scrapes the exporter.
cards.explanation: Prometheus's exporter guidance ties ordinary value collection to the scrape request.

cards.statement: Prometheus exporter guidance accepts caching especially costly values when the exporter documents this in HELP.
cards.explanation: Prometheus permits caching especially costly retrievals when the exporter discloses this in the HELP text.

cards.statement: The Prometheus docs treat request volume, errors and latency as core signals for online-serving systems.
cards.explanation: For online services, request volume, errors and latency expose demand, failures and response time.

cards.statement: The Prometheus docs advise counting requests at their start to align counts with errors and latency.
cards.explanation: Prometheus suggests counting completed requests so request, error and latency statistics share a completion point.
cards.misconception: Request-start counting aligns completion statistics.

cards.statement: Prometheus instrumentation guidance treats the latest successful batch-job time as a key signal.
cards.explanation: The last-success timestamp helps reveal a batch job that has stopped succeeding.

cards.statement: Prometheus guidance delays exporting a known error-counter series until the first error occurs.
cards.explanation: Prometheus advises exposing known series at zero before an event first occurs.
cards.misconception: Known series remain unexported until their first event.

cards.statement: Prometheus guidance uses an event's Unix timestamp as a metric value so PromQL can calculate its age.
cards.explanation: Exporting the event timestamp lets time() - metric calculate age while avoiding periodic age updates.

cards.statement: Prometheus label guidance treats customer email addresses as a suitable dimension for request metrics.
cards.explanation: Prometheus advises bounded dimensions; per-user identifiers create growing label-value sets.
cards.misconception: Growing per-user identifiers are recommended metric labels.

cards.statement: Prometheus exporter guidance chooses HTTP 5xx for partial collection failures that leave useful metrics.
cards.explanation: For useful partial results, Prometheus's exporter guidance prefers an exporter-specific success metric so those results remain available.
cards.misconception: HTTP failure responses are preferred for partial collection failures.

cards.statement: Prometheus guidance reserves the Pushgateway mainly for outcomes of service-level batch jobs.
cards.explanation: The Pushgateway captures batch outcomes that belong to a service rather than a particular machine.

cards.statement: The Pushgateway removes a job's pushed series when the process that pushed them exits.
cards.explanation: The Pushgateway retains pushed series until deletion; the pushing process's exit leaves them stored.
cards.misconception: Pushed metric lifetime follows the originating process.

cards.statement: PromQL time() produces a scalar value when evaluated as an instant query.
cards.explanation: PromQL declares time() with a scalar return type, making it usable where a single numeric argument is expected.

cards.statement: PromQL treats requests_total[5m] as an instant vector of current samples.
cards.explanation: requests_total[5m] yields a range vector containing samples from the selected five-minute window for its series.
cards.misconception: A bracketed time window selects one current sample per series.

cards.statement: Prometheus evaluates a range query at regularly spaced steps across its requested time span.
cards.explanation: A range query repeats the expression at evaluation times separated by the requested step.

cards.statement: Prometheus rejects a scalar-valued root expression in a range query.
cards.explanation: Prometheus accepts scalar expressions such as 5 at the root of a range query.
cards.misconception: Range queries require instant-vector roots.

cards.statement: PromQL's = matcher supports api|web as an alternation between the api and web label values.
cards.explanation: PromQL's = matcher compares literal text; api|web matches that complete label value.
cards.misconception: Equality matchers interpret regex alternation.

cards.statement: PromQL anchors a label regex at the beginning and end of the label value.
cards.explanation: A pattern such as api matches the complete value api; matching a containing string needs a broader pattern.

cards.statement: In Prometheus 3.15.0, a PromQL regex dot matches a newline in a label value.
cards.explanation: Prometheus 3 uses dot-matches-newline behavior for label regexes, including values containing line breaks.

cards.statement: PromQL treats two matchers for the same label name as alternatives.
cards.explanation: PromQL combines same-label matchers with AND: a series must satisfy both.
cards.misconception: Same-label matchers use OR.

cards.statement: PromQL can use {job=~".*"} as a complete vector selector in an ordinary instant query.
cards.explanation: A nameless vector selector needs a matcher that rejects the empty string; .* accepts it.
cards.misconception: A regex selecting arbitrary job values makes a nameless selector valid.

cards.statement: PromQL treats bare on as a keyword even when a stored metric has that name.
cards.explanation: PromQL reserves on for its grammar, so a bare metric selector with that name fails to parse.

cards.statement: PromQL scalar(v) sums the values when v contains two float series.
cards.explanation: With two float elements, scalar(v) returns NaN.
cards.misconception: scalar() aggregates a multi-series float vector.

cards.statement: PromQL vector(5) returns one instant-vector element with an empty label set.
cards.explanation: vector() wraps its scalar argument in a float vector element that carries no labels.

cards.statement: For float counter c, irate(c[5m]) uses the last two samples in the selected window.
cards.explanation: The five-minute range locates recent counter samples; irate() bases its estimate on the final pair.

cards.statement: For float counter c, rate(c[5m]) treats an observed reset inside that window as a negative contribution.
cards.explanation: rate() adjusts observed counter resets before calculating the counter's rate.
cards.misconception: A counter reset subtracts from the rate calculated by rate().

cards.statement: For float counter c, rate(c[5m]) extrapolates observed growth toward the selected window's edges.
cards.explanation: rate() estimates boundary coverage from the sampling interval when scrapes fall near the window edges.

cards.statement: For float counter c, increase(c[5m]) reports the average per-second change over that window.
cards.explanation: increase(c[5m]) reports the change across the window, equivalent to rate(c[5m]) multiplied by the window duration in seconds.
cards.misconception: increase() expresses counter changes per second.

cards.statement: For float counters c, sum(rate(c[5m])) keeps reset correction separate for the contributing series.
cards.explanation: Summing raw counters first can hide a drop in one series behind growth in another.

cards.statement: Prometheus documentation recommends irate() for alerting on slow-moving float counters over five minutes.
cards.explanation: Prometheus documentation favors rate() for alerts and slow counters, since irate() is sensitive to brief spikes.
cards.misconception: The most recent rate estimate is the documented preference for slow-counter alerts.

cards.statement: For float gauge g, delta(g[5m]) extrapolates the first-to-last difference across the selected window.
cards.explanation: delta() adjusts the observed gauge difference to account for sampling coverage at the window edges.

cards.statement: For float gauge g with several samples in 5m, deriv(g[5m]) fits its slope from the two endpoints.
cards.explanation: deriv() fits a line by simple linear regression using the float samples in the selected range.
cards.misconception: deriv() derives its fitted trend from the first and last samples.

cards.statement: resets(h[5m]) can detect loss of a populated bucket in native counter histogram h with unchanged bucket layout.
cards.explanation: A previously populated bucket disappearing from a native counter histogram indicates a reset when its layout stays unchanged.

cards.statement: changes(h[5m]) can count a counter-to-gauge native histogram switch when its values and bucket layout stay identical.
cards.explanation: changes() ignores a counter-to-gauge histogram flavor switch when the histogram contents remain equal.
cards.misconception: Changing a histogram's counter or gauge flavor changes its value for changes().

cards.statement: For float gauge g, avg_over_time(g[5m]) gives equal weight to samples despite irregular spacing.
cards.explanation: avg_over_time() averages sampled values, so densely sampled periods contribute more observations.

cards.statement: For native counter histogram h, rate(h[5m]) returns a float sample for the total observation rate.
cards.explanation: rate(h[5m]) returns a native histogram containing rates for its buckets, observation count and sum.
cards.misconception: rate() converts native histogram samples into observation-count floats.
